reportIntro: The candidates were frozen before any v3 training run started. Only the size of the full-band training pool and the epoch budget vary; the domain ratio, objective, seed and initialisation are inherited unchanged from the rehearsal-heavy candidate that pilot v2 measured. The eligibility gates are the pilot-v1 set, reused unchanged for the fourth consecutive study. The Slakh test split was never used for selection.
frozenBefore: any v3 training run was started

predecessor.outcome: passed every accuracy gate on both domains; rejected on over-segmentation, which the decoder study then fixed with duration-viterbi
predecessor.note: rehearsal-heavy + duration-viterbi is the reference this study must beat. It is already measured under these gates and is NOT retrained.

strategy.description: Keep the rehearsal-heavy recipe exactly and enlarge the Slakh training pool from 120 to 600 compositions, then test whether a longer budget buys more on top.
rationale: Measured: the pilot used 120 of 1289 available train-split compositions - 9 percent. Full-band capability is the axis that survived the p00 confirmation, so more full-band data targets the thing that is actually real.
Measured in pilot v2: every candidate was still improving when the frozen 12-epoch budget ended, so the budget was a binding constraint and its effect is worth separating from the data effect.

The 0.7/0.3 domain ratio is inherited unchanged because it is what preserved solo guitar in pilot v2. At that ratio GuitarSet remains the limiting domain, so per-epoch full-band exposure stays close to the pilot's while being drawn from a five times larger pool - more variety across the run, same rehearsal dominance per epoch.

p00 is spent. This study therefore cannot produce a new performer-level generalisation claim, and its primary axis is full-band accuracy on the held-out Slakh validation subset, which no candidate trains on.

rejectedAlternatives.reason: Changing the ratio and the pool size together would confound them, and the ratio is the one thing pilot v2 demonstrated to be load-bearing for preservation.
Roughly 63 GB of extraction for a first scaling point. 600 is a five-fold increase and answers whether scale helps at all before paying for more.
It was spent under a single-measurement protocol. Measuring it again after seeing a new candidate is precisely what that protocol forbids.

domainSampling.note: Ratio inherited verbatim from the pilot-v2 rehearsal-heavy candidate. Only the pool size changes.
domainSampling.selectionRule: Train compositions are the first N of the deterministic ordering by aligned-MIDI SHA-256, one rendering per composition - the same rule that selected the original 120, so the pilot subset is a strict prefix and the comparison is nested rather than disjoint.

sharedSchedule.seedNote: Same seed as pilots v1 and v2, so differences against rehearsal-heavy are data and budget rather than a different draw.

candidates.note: Identical to pilot-v2 rehearsal-heavy in every respect except the training pool: 600 compositions instead of 120. Isolates data quantity.

The same enlarged pool with double the budget. Isolates whether the 12-epoch ceiling was binding once more data is available. Patience is raised with the budget so early stopping stays proportionate rather than becoming stricter by accident.

evaluation.decoderNote: The decoder selected by the frozen decoder study. Candidates are scored under it, with the production-parity penalty-4 decode reported alongside as a reference point.
evaluation.fullBandDevelopment: Slakh validation subset only; the untouched test split is never used for selection.
evaluation.guitarSetPreservation: p01-p05, both captures. This is a forgetting check and nothing more - see the limitation below.

knownLimitations: p00 IS SPENT. It was measured once under the confirmation protocol and can never again serve as a virgin performer holdout, so this study has no unbiased performer-level generalisation test available and does not claim one.

GuitarSet preservation is measured on p01-p05, which v1 trained on and which every candidate rehearses on. The p00 confirmation showed such gains are substantially a rehearsal effect, so GuitarSet accuracy movements here should be read as forgetting checks only.
Reference labels for Slakh are note-level, so the full-band fragmentation gate remains not-evaluable.
Slakh2100 is rendered from MIDI, so all full-band evidence remains synthetic-domain and does not establish production readiness.
The enlarged pool is a strict superset of the pilot's, so the two are nested rather than independent samples.
